newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INSIGHT - NZ dollar drifts lower with Aust. dollar.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NZ dollar drifts lower with Aust. dollar.

text.p: Post-budget weakness in the Australian dollar weighed on its New Zealand counterpart in early Wednesday trade.
In the absence of fresh domestic data, dealers were looking to the majors for fresh influences.
However, they said they were also keeping a watching brief on parliament's privileges committee expected today.
Almost two months after its first hearing, the committee is expected to deliver its verdict on Treasurer Winston Peters' fracas in parliament with National MP John Banks.
The report was due to be tabled in Parliament this afternoon with the House expected to debate it on Thursday morning.
By 9 a.m. (2100 GMT) the Kiwi was at 0.6940/47, down slightly from its 0.6943/50 open and compared with its 0.6955/62 close on Tuesday.
"It's been a pretty quiet session and, with no data out today, I suppose the only thing to watch for some life is the (U.S.) dollar or the Aussie," said one dealer.
"Or maybe Mr Peters or Mr Banks will have something, but it looks as it that will fizzle out to nothing," he said.
"I think we'll be looking to other markets for direction here today," he said.
The Kiwi was expected to trade a 0.6930-60 range on the day.
The Australian dollar was at US$0.7760/65, down sharply from 0.7826/31 just before Tuesday's budget.
Australian commentators complained that the budget had not done enough in terms of spending cuts and as a result could not justify seeking a credit rating upgrade for the country.
